_note: Semester project catalog. Students rank three preferences; the instructor assigns one project per student (at most two students per project, with different scopes). difficulty: 1 (approachable) … 3 (ambitious).

themes.title: Text and ciphers
themes.blurb: Strings, loops and arrays in C. Small programs with a big history.

projects.title: Cipher toolkit
projects.summary: A command-line tool that encrypts and decrypts text with Caesar, Vigenère and substitution ciphers.
projects.min: Caesar and Vigenère, both directions, with input validation and clear usage messages.
projects.advanced: A cracker: break a Caesar or substitution cipher automatically with letter-frequency analysis, and show the top three candidate plaintexts.

projects.title: Readability and word statistics
projects.summary: Read any text file and report its grade level (Coleman–Liau), word counts, longest words and sentence lengths.
projects.min: Coleman–Liau index, word/sentence/letter counts, the ten most frequent words.
projects.advanced: Compare two texts side by side and a histogram of word lengths drawn in the terminal; bonus: n-gram based next-word suggestion.

projects.title: Wordle in the terminal
projects.summary: The daily word game, playable in the terminal with colored feedback and a dictionary file.
projects.min: Random secret word, six guesses, green/yellow/gray feedback, win/lose message, only dictionary words accepted.
projects.advanced: A solver that ranks candidate guesses by how much they narrow the remaining word list, and statistics over 100 simulated games.

themes.title: Algorithms
themes.blurb: Searching, sorting and problem solving, with running time you can measure.

projects.title: Sorting visualizer
projects.summary: Implement sorting algorithms in C, log every step, and replay the steps as an animation in the browser.
projects.min: Three sorts in C that write each comparison and swap to a file; a timing table for n = 1 000, 10 000, 100 000.
projects.advanced: A web page that animates the logged steps as bars; add quicksort and a chart of time versus n.

projects.title: Election simulator
projects.summary: Count ballots under plurality, instant-runoff and a pairwise (Condorcet) method, and show that the winner can differ.
projects.min: Plurality and instant-runoff from a ballot file, with tie handling and a readable report.
projects.advanced: Tideman (ranked pairs) with cycle detection, and a generator of random elections where the three methods disagree.

projects.title: Maze generator and solver
projects.summary: Generate random mazes and solve them, printing the path in the terminal or as an image.
projects.min: Random maze of any size (recursive backtracker), BFS solver, ASCII output with the path marked.
projects.advanced: A* with a heuristic, a step counter comparing BFS/DFS/A*, and PNG/BMP output.

themes.title: Memory, files and images
themes.blurb: Bytes, pointers and binary files. The most ‘under the hood’ projects.

projects.title: Image filters
projects.summary: Apply grayscale, sepia, mirror, blur and edge-detection filters to BMP images.
projects.min: Grayscale, sepia, reflect and blur on 24-bit BMP files, chosen with a command-line flag.
projects.advanced: Sobel edge detection, a pixelate/mosaic filter and an ASCII-art exporter.

projects.title: File recovery
projects.summary: Recover deleted JPEG files from a raw memory-card image by scanning for their signatures.
projects.min: Read a raw image in 512-byte blocks, detect JPEG headers, write each recovered file as NNN.jpg.
projects.advanced: Also recover PNG files, print a summary (count, total bytes) and verify with a checksum.

projects.title: Hexdump and file inspector
projects.summary: Your own `xxd`: show any file as hex and ASCII, and guess its type from magic bytes.
projects.min: Hex + ASCII dump with offsets, options for width and range, detection of PNG/JPEG/PDF/ZIP/ELF by signature.
projects.advanced: Parse and print the header fields of BMP and PNG files, and a byte-frequency chart (entropy estimate).

themes.title: Data structures
themes.blurb: Linked lists, hash tables and tries. Speed and memory trade-offs you can feel.

projects.title: Spell checker
projects.summary: Load a 140 000-word dictionary into a hash table and spell-check a text as fast as possible.
projects.min: Load, check, size and unload with no memory leaks; report misspelled words and timings.
projects.advanced: Compare two hash functions and bucket counts with a timing table; suggest corrections with edit distance 1.

projects.title: Student records manager
projects.summary: Add, search, update and delete records kept in a linked list and saved to a file.
projects.min: Menu-driven CRUD on a linked list with save/load, sorted listing and search by name or ID.
projects.advanced: A binary search tree index for fast lookup, CSV import/export and simple statistics.

projects.title: Autocomplete with a trie
projects.summary: Type a prefix, get the words that start with it, instantly, from a trie built from a word list.
projects.min: Build a trie from a dictionary, print all completions of a prefix, free all memory.
projects.advanced: Rank completions by word frequency from a text corpus and support deletion.

themes.title: Python, AI and data
themes.blurb: Higher-level languages and real data. For students who want to build tools they will actually use.

projects.title: Personal finance tracker
projects.summary: Import bank CSV exports, categorize spending and produce monthly reports.
projects.min: CSV import into SQLite, category rules, monthly totals per category printed as a table.
projects.advanced: Charts with matplotlib, budget alerts and a tiny web dashboard with Flask.

projects.title: Unbeatable tic-tac-toe
projects.summary: A game AI that never loses, using the minimax algorithm.
projects.min: Playable game against a minimax AI that never loses; a mode where the AI plays itself.
projects.advanced: Connect Four with alpha-beta pruning and a depth limit, plus a count of explored nodes.

projects.title: Handwritten digit classifier from scratch
projects.summary: Recognize handwritten digits with k-nearest neighbors written by you, no ML library.
projects.min: k-NN on a small MNIST CSV, accuracy on a test split, a confusion matrix.
projects.advanced: A tiny neural network (one hidden layer) trained with plain numpy, and a comparison with k-NN.

projects.title: Course assistant chatbot
projects.summary: A chatbot that answers questions about this course using an LLM API and the course notes as context.
projects.min: Command-line chat with a system prompt, the week notes injected as context, and refusal when the answer is not in the notes.
projects.advanced: Simple retrieval (chunking + keyword or embedding search), a test set of 20 questions with scores, and a web interface.

themes.title: The web
themes.blurb: Things people can click. HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with an optional Python backend.

projects.title: Typing-speed trainer
projects.summary: A web page that measures words per minute and accuracy, and remembers your progress.
projects.min: Random text, live WPM and accuracy, error highlighting, history saved in localStorage.
projects.advanced: Difficulty levels, a chart of progress over time, and a Flask + SQLite leaderboard.

projects.title: Password strength and breach checker
projects.summary: Rate a password’s strength, estimate crack time, and check it against known breaches without ever sending it.
projects.min: Strength meter with entropy estimate and rules, crack-time estimate at several guess rates.
projects.advanced: k-anonymity breach check (Have I Been Pwned range API) and a C program that brute-forces short passwords to show the numbers are real.

projects.title: Campus event board
projects.summary: A small web app where students post and browse campus events.
projects.min: List, add and delete events stored in SQLite, with server-side validation.
projects.advanced: User accounts with sessions, search and filters, and an .ics export.

projects.title: Pixel-art editor
projects.summary: Draw pixel art in the browser and export it as a real image file.
projects.min: Grid editor with palette, undo and PNG export via canvas.
projects.advanced: Export/import the 24-bit BMP format written by your own C code (bridging week 6 and week 12).
